stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
passage: Researchers at a Chilean observatory announced in 2024 that they had detected an unusual pattern of radio emissions from a white dwarf star designated LP 40-365, located roughly 98 light-years from Earth. Unlike typical white dwarfs, which emit little detectable radio energy, LP 40-365 produced periodic bursts at 1.4 gigahertz intervals that lasted approximately eleven seconds each. The team attributed these bursts to the star's extraordinarily rapid rotation — it completes one full revolution every 8.9 minutes — which generates a magnetic field strong enough to accelerate charged particles along its poles, producing focused beams of radio waves.

options.text: A white dwarf star near Earth has been found to emit unusual radio bursts, which researchers attribute to its exceptionally fast rotation and the resulting magnetic field.
White dwarf stars are generally unable to produce radio emissions because they lack the rotational speed needed to generate magnetic fields.
The Chilean observatory that detected LP 40-365's emissions specializes in monitoring stars within 100 light-years of Earth.
Charged particles accelerated along a star's poles always produce radio waves at a frequency of 1.4 gigahertz.

explanation: The passage describes the detection of unusual radio bursts from white dwarf LP 40-365 and explains that these bursts are caused by the star's rapid rotation generating a strong magnetic field. The option about surprising radio bursts linked to fast rotation captures this central point. The option claiming white dwarfs generally cannot produce radio emissions overstates what the passage says — the text notes that typical white dwarfs emit little detectable radio energy, not that they are unable to do so. The option about the observatory's specialization fabricates information not present in the passage. The option asserting that pole-accelerated particles always produce 1.4-gigahertz radio waves generalizes a single observation into a universal rule unsupported by the text.

stem: According to the text, what is the main reason Okoro and Petersen proposed to explain the disparity they observed?
passage: Industrial ecologists Chidinma Okoro and Lars Petersen analyzed municipal recycling data from 47 cities across seven West African nations between 2016 and 2022. They found that cities with populations under 250,000 recycled an average of 31% of their plastic waste, while cities exceeding one million residents recycled only 14%. Okoro and Petersen attributed this gap primarily to differences in waste collection infrastructure: smaller cities tended to rely on decentralized, community-operated sorting cooperatives that processed materials close to the point of generation, whereas larger cities depended on centralized facilities that required long-haul transport of unsorted waste — a process in which significant quantities of recyclable material were lost to contamination or diverted to landfills before reaching the processing stage.

options.text: Larger cities generate proportionally more non-recyclable plastic types than smaller cities due to differences in consumer purchasing patterns.

The decentralized collection systems common in smaller cities process waste closer to its source, reducing material loss, while centralized systems in larger cities lose recyclable material during long-distance transport.
Smaller cities benefit from stronger government regulations requiring residents to sort plastic waste before collection.
Recycling cooperatives in smaller cities receive more international funding per capita than centralized facilities in larger cities.

explanation: The passage explicitly states that Okoro and Petersen attributed the recycling disparity to differences in waste collection infrastructure — specifically that decentralized cooperatives in smaller cities process waste near its source, while centralized facilities in larger cities lose recyclable material during long-haul transport. The option about non-recyclable plastic types and consumer purchasing patterns introduces factors not discussed in the passage. The option about stronger government regulations is unsupported; the passage does not mention regulatory differences. The option about international funding introduces an economic factor that the passage never addresses.

stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
passage: Musicologist Farah Nassiri-Khorasani has argued that the rhythmic structures of early twentieth-century Persian classical music were more fluid than previously recognized. Analyzing 162 wax cylinder recordings made between 1906 and 1928 in Tehran and Isfahan, she found that performers routinely shifted between duple and triple meters within a single dastgah performance — a practice that later pedagogical treatises, written primarily in the 1950s and 1960s, described as incorrect or unorthodox. Nassiri-Khorasani contends that these treatises, which became the standard references for conservatory instruction, imposed a retrospective rigidity on the tradition by codifying norms that reflected mid-century aesthetic preferences rather than historical performance practice. She suggests that the wax cylinder evidence reveals a pre-codification era in which metric flexibility was not a deviation but a defining characteristic of the art form.

options.text: Wax cylinder recordings from early twentieth-century Iran demonstrate that rhythmic flexibility was a standard feature of Persian classical music before later pedagogical treatises imposed stricter metric conventions.
The 1950s treatises on Persian classical music were written by scholars who had never heard the wax cylinder recordings from the early 1900s.
Performers in Tehran and Isfahan between 1906 and 1928 preferred triple meter over duple meter in most dastgah performances.
Farah Nassiri-Khorasani has proposed that conservatory instruction in Persian classical music should return to using wax cylinder recordings as primary teaching materials.

explanation: The passage's central argument is that early recordings show rhythmic flexibility was standard practice in Persian classical music, and that later treatises retrospectively imposed rigidity that did not reflect the historical tradition. The option about wax cylinder evidence revealing pre-codification metric flexibility captures this main idea. The option claiming treatise authors never heard the recordings introduces a biographical claim nowhere stated in the passage. The option about performers preferring triple meter misrepresents the text, which describes performers shifting between duple and triple meters, not favoring one over the other. The option about Nassiri-Khorasani proposing wax cylinders as teaching materials goes beyond the passage — she argues the recordings reveal historical practice, but the text does not describe any specific pedagogical recommendation.

stem: Which quotation from an art historian, if true, would most directly support the claim that Osorio's sculptural technique was influenced by traditional Oaxacan woodcarving?
passage: The Mexican-American sculptor Diego Osorio gained recognition in the 1990s for large-scale wooden figures carved from single blocks of reclaimed Douglas fir. Art critics have noted that Osorio's technique of leaving visible tool marks on finished surfaces and applying water-based aniline dyes in vivid, contrasting colors bears a strong resemblance to the methods used by Oaxacan alebrije carvers, who produce brightly painted fantastical animal figures. Osorio himself has acknowledged spending several formative months in Oaxaca as a young apprentice, though he has characterized his mature work as distinct from the alebrije tradition.

options.text: "Osorio's palette of aniline dyes and his deliberate preservation of chisel strokes directly echo the surface treatment characteristic of Oaxacan alebrije workshops, where he trained in his early twenties."
"The monumental scale of Osorio's figures sets his work apart from virtually all contemporary woodcarving traditions in the Americas."
"Reclaimed Douglas fir is rarely used in Oaxacan carving, which traditionally relies on the soft wood of the copal tree."
"Osorio's decision to depict human figures rather than animals represents a clear departure from the alebrije tradition."

explanation: The claim concerns Oaxacan influence on Osorio's technique. The quotation connecting his aniline dye palette and preserved chisel strokes directly to Oaxacan alebrije workshop methods, and confirming his training there, provides the most direct support. The quotation about monumental scale distinguishing his work addresses what makes him different, not what links him to Oaxacan traditions. The quotation about different wood species highlights a material distinction between Osorio and Oaxacan carvers, which would weaken rather than support the influence claim. The quotation about depicting human figures rather than animals points to a departure from the alebrije tradition, which again does not support the claim of influence.

stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the researchers' hypothesis?
passage: Geochemists at a Norwegian university studying sediment cores from Lake Torneträsk in northern Sweden noticed that layers deposited between 536 and 545 CE contained concentrations of volcanic sulfate aerosols roughly four times higher than those in adjacent centuries. The researchers hypothesized that sustained volcanic aerosol loading during this decade suppressed summer temperatures in Scandinavia enough to shorten the growing season for barley, the primary cereal crop of the region's early medieval communities, potentially triggering the widespread settlement abandonments documented in archaeological surveys of the area.

options.text: Pollen records from Lake Torneträsk sediments show a sharp decline in barley pollen between 536 and 545 CE, followed by a gradual recovery after 560 CE.
Volcanic sulfate aerosols in Antarctic ice cores from the same period are present at concentrations even higher than those found in Lake Torneträsk.
Archaeological surveys have determined that the settlements abandoned near Lake Torneträsk were reoccupied by different cultural groups around 620 CE.
Barley cultivation in modern northern Sweden remains viable at summer temperatures up to two degrees Celsius below current averages.

explanation: The hypothesis proposes a causal chain from volcanic aerosols to suppressed temperatures to shortened barley growing seasons to settlement abandonment. Pollen records showing a sharp decline in barley pollen during precisely the period of elevated aerosol loading would directly support the link between aerosol-driven cooling and reduced barley cultivation. The finding about Antarctic ice core concentrations addresses the global extent of volcanism but does not connect aerosol loading to barley or settlements in Scandinavia. The finding about later reoccupation by different groups addresses post-abandonment history without bearing on what caused the original abandonment. The finding about modern barley viability at lower temperatures would actually weaken the hypothesis by suggesting barley can tolerate cooling, undermining the proposed mechanism.

stem: Which finding from the study, if accurate, would most directly undermine the researchers' conclusion?
passage: A 2023 study of 114 sixteenth-century Portuguese nautical charts concluded that the systematic westward displacement of the African coastline visible in charts produced after 1502 was a deliberate cartographic strategy rather than an accumulation of navigational errors. The researchers argued that Portuguese chartmakers, under instructions from the crown, intentionally shifted the coastline to make the demarcation line established by the Treaty of Tordesillas appear to encompass more of the South American landmass within Portugal's territorial claim. The study supported this argument by noting that the displacement appeared abruptly and uniformly across charts from multiple workshops, a pattern inconsistent with gradual error accumulation.

options.text: Charts produced by Spanish cartographers during the same period display a comparable westward shift in the African coastline, despite Spain having no incentive to enlarge Portugal's territorial claim.
Portuguese crown records from the early 1500s include correspondence discussing the strategic importance of the Tordesillas demarcation line.
Navigational instruments available to Portuguese sailors in the early sixteenth century were less accurate for longitude measurements than for latitude measurements.
Several charts produced before 1502 by the same workshops show minor, inconsistent westward displacements attributable to copying errors.

explanation: The researchers' conclusion rests on the claim that Portuguese chartmakers deliberately shifted the African coastline to benefit Portugal's territorial claim under the Treaty of Tordesillas. If Spanish cartographers — who had no reason to enlarge Portugal's claim — independently produced the same displacement, the shift cannot be explained by deliberate Portuguese strategy and more likely reflects a common technical or methodological factor, directly undermining the conclusion. The finding about Portuguese crown correspondence discussing the Tordesillas line would strengthen rather than undermine the conclusion by showing official interest in the boundary. The finding about longitude inaccuracy addresses general navigational limitations but does not explain the abrupt and uniform appearance of the displacement that the study identified. The finding about pre-1502 copying errors shows minor inconsistencies before the critical date but does not challenge the post-1502 pattern that forms the study's primary evidence.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
passage: The painted bunting (Passerina ciris) is among the most vividly colored songbirds in North America, with males displaying bright blue, green, and red plumage. Despite this conspicuous appearance, painted buntings are remarkably difficult to observe in the wild. Field researchers conducting breeding surveys in coastal South Carolina between 2018 and 2023 reported that they detected 83% of territorial males by song alone, without ever achieving a visual sighting. This finding suggests that ________

options.text: painted buntings tend to sing and forage within dense vegetation that conceals them despite their vivid coloration.
the bright plumage of male painted buntings is primarily useful for attracting mates during nighttime displays.
female painted buntings are easier to observe in the field than males because their plumage is less conspicuous.
territorial male painted buntings sing less frequently during the breeding season than during migration.

explanation: The passage notes that despite vivid coloring, most males were detected by sound rather than sight. The most logical explanation is that the birds inhabit dense cover that hides them visually, reconciling their bright plumage with their low visual detection rate. The option about nighttime displays introduces an unsupported claim — the passage provides no information about when displays occur, and nighttime activity would not explain daytime detection by song. The option about females being easier to observe introduces a comparison not addressed in the passage, and less conspicuous plumage would logically make females harder, not easier, to spot. The option about reduced singing during breeding contradicts the passage's implication that song is the primary detection method during breeding surveys.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
passage: Historians examining parish registers from seventeenth-century Cornwall have found that the surnames of tin miners' families were distributed across parishes in patterns closely matching the locations of known tin lode deposits. However, the surnames of families involved in the wool trade — which was equally prevalent in Cornwall during this period — showed no comparable geographic clustering and instead appeared in roughly equal proportions throughout the county. The historians concluded that ________

options.text: tin mining tied families to specific locations dictated by the geology of ore deposits, whereas the wool trade allowed families to operate from any location with adequate grazing land, which was widely available across Cornwall.
wool trading families in seventeenth-century Cornwall changed their surnames more frequently than tin mining families, making geographic tracking of wool families unreliable.
tin mining was a more profitable occupation than wool trading in seventeenth-century Cornwall, which explains why mining families remained in fixed locations.
parish registers in Cornwall were more carefully maintained in mining communities than in wool-trading communities during the seventeenth century.

explanation: The passage contrasts the geographic clustering of mining surnames near ore deposits with the even distribution of wool-trade surnames. The logical conclusion is that mining required proximity to fixed geological resources, while wool trading could be conducted anywhere grazing land was available — and Cornwall had grazing land throughout the county. The option about wool families changing surnames introduces an unsupported claim about naming practices not mentioned in the passage. The option about mining profitability introduces an economic factor the passage does not discuss, and higher income does not logically explain geographic fixity. The option about differential record-keeping quality suggests the data itself is unreliable, which contradicts the historians' willingness to draw conclusions from the registers.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
passage: Cognitive scientist Yumi Takahashi conducted experiments in which 203 bilingual Japanese-English speakers were asked to estimate the duration of animated events shown on a screen. When tested in Japanese, participants consistently estimated event durations as shorter than participants tested in English, even when viewing identical animations. Takahashi noted that the Japanese language more frequently encodes events using grammatical constructions that emphasize completion — verb endings that mark an action as finished — whereas English more often uses progressive constructions that frame actions as ongoing. She argued that these grammatical differences do not merely reflect different ways of describing events but actively shape temporal cognition, leading her to conclude that ________

options.text: speakers of languages that grammatically emphasize event completion may systematically perceive events as occupying less time than speakers of languages that emphasize event continuation.
bilingual individuals always estimate event durations more accurately in their first language than in their second language.
Japanese grammatical constructions are inherently more efficient than English constructions for describing timed events.
temporal estimation accuracy improves significantly when participants are tested in a language they learned after age twelve.

explanation: The passage describes a study in which language of testing influenced temporal estimates: Japanese (with completion-oriented grammar) led to shorter duration estimates than English (with continuation-oriented grammar). Takahashi argued that grammar actively shapes temporal cognition, so the logical conclusion is that languages emphasizing completion cause speakers to perceive events as shorter. The option about bilingual individuals being more accurate in their first language introduces a claim about accuracy and language order that the passage does not address — the study compared languages, not proficiency levels. The option about Japanese being inherently more efficient mischaracterizes the finding as one about linguistic efficiency rather than about how grammar shapes perception. The option about age of acquisition and estimation accuracy introduces a variable the passage never mentions.
